**Gastroscopy** (Danish: *gastroskopi*) is a medical procedure that plays a critical role in the diagnostic workup of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) for children and young people in Denmark. According to the DANIBD 2025 report, it is a mandatory component of the recommended clinical evaluation defined by [[indikator-1b|Indikator 1b]] [^src1]. The procedure is specifically used to assess the upper gastrointestinal system, supplementing [[koloskopi|colonoscopy]] to ensure a comprehensive diagnostic approach [^src1].

Within the Danish national quality development strategy for IBD, which is driven by the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Program (RKKP) and administered via the DANIBD database, gastroscopy is a key metric for evaluating the completeness of patient workups [^src1]. The strict criteria for a complete diagnostic workup under Indicator 1b require that diagnoses are established by a combination of procedures: specifically, gastroscopy (with or without biopsy) AND colonoscopy AND an MRI of the small intestine or capsule endoscopy [^src2]. 

The implementation of these evidence-based diagnostic recommendations has shown significant regional and local variation across Denmark [^src1]. In response to clinical discussions, systemic challenges such as miscoding, and new international guidelines, a major policy change has been agreed upon. Moving forward, the requirements for [[indikator-1b|Indikator 1b]] will be adjusted to only mandate gastroscopy and colonoscopy, illustrating how registry data directly drives evidence-based practice changes and quality improvement in the Danish healthcare system [^src2].
